name: Presidente InterContinental Mexico City
positioning: InterContinental Presidente Mexico City is a 42-floor tower in the heart of Polanco, steps from the Anthropology Museum, Reforma and Chapultepec, with rooms looking over Bosque de Chapultepec, the Hela Spa and a Japanese speakeasy.
best_for: Travelers who want city and park views from a high-rise room
Visitors to Chapultepec, the Anthropology Museum and the Auditorio Nacional

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Polanco, a district known for diplomatic headquarters, renowned restaurants, museums and shopping.
The hotel is just steps from the Anthropology Museum, Reforma and Chapultepec.
The hotel is steps from the Auditorio Nacional.
The hotel is close to Presidente Masaryk, an avenue well known for luxury shopping.
The hotel rises 42 floors, which gives it impressive views.
The grand entrance is centered around a contemporary sculpture.
The presidential suites are named after Diego Rivera, Jose C Orozco and David A Siqueiros.
Epicentro is a gin and tonic bar with caviar, champagne, a wide tequila selection and live music.
Amaral is a fine-dining restaurant inspired by the cuisines of the Mediterranean: French, Spanish, Italian and Greek.
The hotel has children's activities onsite.
Pets are welcome, including dogs and cats.
The hotel has EarthCheck sustainability certification.

highlights.text: Each room has a pane of glass nearly the width of the room, giving panoramic views of the city.
The guest rooms look out over Bosque de Chapultepec.
Hela Spa offers Nordic massages, body treatments, oxygenating facials and deep cleansing.
Tokoya Nigiri Bar is an intimate Japanese speakeasy in what was once a barbershop, pairing traditional Japanese cuisine with craft cocktails.

considerations.text: The hotel does not have a pool.
Benito Juarez International Airport is about 18 kilometers from the hotel.
WhataHotel notes an urban setting with busy city traffic and noise.
